clearedSpotChecks.check: Assumption A1 on World Chain: does transient storage end at the transaction boundary (critic gap of cycle 5).
clearedSpotChecks.note: I reran the probe on 2026-11-24 with eth_simulateV1 and my own bytecode: a first call runs TSTORE(0,1), a second call in the same simulated block returns TLOAD(0), and a third contract does TSTORE then TLOAD in one call as a positive control. On https://480.rpc.thirdweb.com and https://sparkling-autumn-dinghy.worldchain-mainnet.quiknode.pro the second call returned 0 and the control returned 1. The same result came from the endpoints of OP Mainnet, Base, Unichain, Zora, Ink and Soneium listed in networks.json. The unlock flag is a transient slot set and cleared in one call (src/libraries/Lock.sol:10-27, src/PoolManager.sol:104-114), and the delta count is checked before lock at src/PoolManager.sol:112. A flag or delta left over from an earlier transaction would let a later caller pass the isUnlocked check, and the probe shows none is left over in the simulation path. The probe covers eth_simulateV1, which uses the same revm journal as block production; it does not cover a mined block.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Rerun of pmdiff.py, 250 scripts with the deployed PoolManager bytecode placed at one address under identical state, compared with Ethereum.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I did not rerun the 250 scripts. I checked that the bytecode they rest on is the same program on every chain. eth_getCode on the seven PoolManagers and on Ethereum's 0x000000000004444c5dc75cB358380D2e3dE08A90 gives 24,009 bytes on six chains, differing from Ethereum only in the 20 bytes at offsets 13,618 to 13,637, which hold the chain's own PoolManager address (the immutable copy of address(this)). Unichain's predeploy at 0x1f98400000000000000000000000000000000004 has 24,050 bytes; a byte alignment shows the same address substitution and a different trailer from offset 23,997, where Unichain carries a 0xa2 CBOR map with an IPFS metadata hash and the others a 0xa1 map with only the solc version. The trailer follows the final INVALID and is never executed, so the executable code is identical on all seven chains and the pmdiff comparison tests the code that holds user funds.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Does Base replace or wrap any EVM instruction at v1.5.6.
clearedSpotChecks.note: crates/common/evm/src/evm.rs at tag v1.5.6 declares the table type as EthInstructions (lines 37, 125), but the type alone does not exclude a table edited at build time. I read crates/common/evm/src/api/builder.rs at the same tag: both constructors set instruction to EthInstructions::new_mainnet_with_spec(spec.into()) (lines 104 and 122) with no insert_instruction call afterwards. The handler in crates/common/evm/src/handler.rs changes gas settlement of the last frame (lines 198-240) and the caller reimbursement, which changes how much gas is charged, not what an opcode or a call returns to the PoolManager. No arithmetic, jump, memory or transient storage instruction is replaced on Base.
